answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph, with voting weight inherited from trusted starting nodes rather than created by new identities. A Sybil cluster—whether its nodes are named shale, wharf, or sable—can gain influence only through its links to the trusted region. If that boundary is sparse, the cluster has low conductance and a low escape probability; with capped propagation and finite walk length, its aggregate voting weight is bounded by the trust entering across the cut, limiting gains from internal sybil-to-sybil attestations.
